description: HTTP header names and prefixes with Ferrum Edge semantics: gateway assertions, diagnostic response headers, internal markers, mesh control headers, and admin API headers, including standard HTTP ETag and If-Match. Names and prefixes match case-insensitively. Availability records the first Edge tag containing the surface. From Edge v0.9.15 the gateway writes its request assertions after it has resolved a client's Connection nominations at HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/3 ingress; the src/proxy/headers.rs provenance note gives the rule.

provenance.note: Connection nominations (ferrum-edge#6090, issue #6087, from v0.9.15): HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/3 ingress removes every field a client's Connection header nominates before any plugin runs, and rewrites Connection to keep only the close option and the request hop-by-hop names connection, keep-alive, proxy-authorization, proxy-connection, te, trailer, transfer-encoding and upgrade. Host, Content-Length, Expect, Forwarded, X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Port, X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Real-IP and the configured FERRUM_REAL_IP_HEADER are protected and keep their client values for routing, framing and trusted-proxy client-IP resolution. A nominated Authorization is removed before authentication. Gateway assertions (consumer identity, X-Authenticated-Identity, claim_headers destinations, X-Geo-Country, path-param captures) and transformer-added headers are written afterwards, so a client nomination cannot remove them. HTTP/2 rejects Connection and is unchanged. Gateway-owned assertion names match ASCII case-insensitively with _ equivalent to - (field_names_equivalent_for_backends), the folding CGI-style backends apply. From v0.9.17, enabled X-Ferrum-Hops is stamped before confinement and protected from Connection nominations, then reasserted after mutable hook phases; the zero-disable passthrough rule is described in its entry.

not_headers.note: OpenAPI document extension fields read by the API-spec import (docs/api_specs.md), not HTTP headers.

headers.name: x-ferrum-peer-spiffe-id
headers.edge_behavior: With spiffe_identity forward_identity=true (default false), the before_proxy hook removes every client copy using ASCII case-insensitive names with _ equivalent to -, then writes the admitted peer SPIFFE ID if present. With forwarding disabled the hook does not mutate this header. HTTP family only; the shared request-trailer boundary always drops client copies through its folded x-ferrum-* rule. require_identity and allowed_trust_domains govern admission independently.

headers.name: x-ferrum-source-principal
headers.edge_behavior: Authenticated source SPIFFE ID after a trusted HBONE assertor baggage rewrite. Stamped on mesh_authz CUSTOM provider checks, after removing any selected copy; absent when the gateway has no corresponding identity, never empty. Provider admission refuses all x-ferrum-* names in includeRequestHeadersInCheck and includeAdditionalHeadersInCheck, so client values cannot supply these assertions. These are check-request headers, not automatic backend identity headers.
